text: Write an annotation that survives to run time, and read it. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class Row { @Column("acct_id") long id; long ignored; }
explanation: Verified: `id -> acct_id`, and `ignored` is skipped. Change the retention to the default and the loop finds nothing — everything compiles and no error appears, which is the commonest annotation bug. That enumerate-check-act pattern is essentially all of how an object-relational mapper works, and the single-member-named-`value` convention is why so many annotations have a member with that unhelpful name.
